Sources and extraction: Vendor-reported numbers cover each vendor's own models only; competitor columns in vendor tables are not recorded.
Some vendors publish benchmark tables only as images; those values were transcribed from the images.
When a vendor page could not be read, numbers relayed by a secondary site are stored as aggregator rows, the lowest priority.
Effort 'unknown' means the source does not state the reasoning effort; 'default' means the model's default setting.
Benchmark versions are stored separately (for example Terminal-Bench 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0, OSWorld 2.0 / 2.1, GDPval-AA versions) and are merged into one family only for ranking.
Elo-based boards (Arena, Design Arena, GDPval-AA, AA Briefcase) are re-fitted over time, so a model's Elo can change without a new run.

The harness matters: the same model can differ by several points between vendor CLIs (Claude Code, Codex CLI) and neutral harnesses (mini-swe-agent, Terminus 2). The harness is stored with every score.
Artificial Analysis component scores come from its comparison pages and are rounded to integers.
Arena numbers come from the official lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset on Hugging Face; snapshot dates are in each row's note.
Terminal-Bench boards are read from the maintainers' server-rendered mirrors, because the official pages render client-side.
Saturated boards (for example the SWE-Bench Pro V2 full split and MMMU-Pro) count at half weight in rankings; harder subsets are more informative.
Boards that are no longer maintained are marked stale and excluded from rankings.
